title: Compatible affine charts and the flat stalk locus
statement: Let $S,X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $p:X\to S$, $q:Y\to S$, $f:X\to Y$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every $x\in X$ there exist affine open neighbourhoods $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $p(x)$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset q^{-1}(W)$ of $f(x)$, and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset p^{-1}(W)\cap f^{-1}(V)$ of $x$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that the induced ring maps $A\to B\to C$ make $B$ finite type over $A$ and $C$ finitely presented over both $A$ and $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For every $z\in Z$, let $\mathfrak r\subset C$ be its prime and $\mathfrak b\subset B$ its inverse image. The canonical identifications $\mathcal O_{X,z}\cong C_{\mathfrak r}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y,f(z)}\cong B_{\mathfrak b}$ identify the stalk map of $f$ with the localization of $B\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The subset $E=\{\mathfrak r\in\operatorname{Spec}C:C_{\mathfrak r}\text{ is flat as a }B\text{-module}\}$ is open [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and under $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$ its points are exactly the $z\in Z$ where $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. No flatness hypothesis on $p$ is required.

proof.text:
Fix $x\in X$. By the affine-opens basis lemma choose an affine open $W
i p(x)$, then an affine open $V
i f(x)$ inside the open $q^{-1}(W)$, and then an affine open $Z
i x$ inside the open $p^{-1}(W)\cap f^{-1}(V)$. We choose an affine refinement of this intersection; we do not assert that the intersection is affine. Write their section rings as $A,B,C$. Restriction of the structure-sheaf maps gives $A	o B	o C$; their composite is the map induced by $p$, since $q\circ f=p$ and the sheaf maps commute with restrictions. The affine-spectrum dictionary identifies these opens with the indicated spectra.

Apply the finite-presentation cancellation lemma to the given $S$-morphism $f$: its hypotheses are exactly that $p$ is locally of finite presentation and $q$ is locally of finite type. Thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation. The all-affine-pairs lemmas now apply to $(q,V,W)$, $(p,Z,W)$ and $(f,Z,V)$, respectively. They give that $B$ is finite type over $A$, $C$ is finitely presented over $A$, and $C$ is finitely presented over $B$. All three required image containments were built into step 1.

Let $\varphi:B\to C$ be the chart map and let $z\in Z$ correspond to $\mathfrak r$. The affine-spectrum morphism sends $\mathfrak r$ to $\mathfrak b=\varphi^{-1}\mathfrak r$, so $f(z)$ has that prime in $V$. The affine-open stalk-localization lemma gives $C_{\mathfrak r}\cong\mathcal O_{X,z}$ and $B_{\mathfrak b}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,f(z)}$, sending fractions to the corresponding quotients of germs. The stalk map sends the germ of $b\in B$ to the germ of $\varphi(b)$ by the definition of a sheaf morphism. Consequently it sends $b/t$ to $\varphi(b)/\varphi(t)$ for $t\notin\mathfrak b$; here $\varphi(t)\notin\mathfrak r$. Every fraction has this form, which proves the asserted identification of the entire stalk map.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves (6)); stalk map evaluated on germs and inverses

proof.text: Use openness of flatness with base ring $B$, finitely presented $B$-algebra $C$ from step 2, and module $M=C$. This module is finitely presented over itself: it has one generator $1$ and no relations, or the presentation $C^0\to C\to C\to0$ with the last map the identity. Its localization at $\mathfrak r$ is exactly $C_{\mathfrak r}$. The cited theorem therefore says exactly that $E=\{\mathfrak r:C_{\mathfrak r}\text{ is flat over }B\}$ is open.

The localized ring $C_{\mathfrak r}$ is a $B_{\mathfrak b}$-module via the map in step 3, since every $t\in B\setminus\mathfrak b$ maps to a unit. Apply flatness over a localization with $A=B$, $W=B\setminus\mathfrak b$, $A\prime=B_{\mathfrak b}$ and $M=C_{\mathfrak r}$. It gives flatness over $B$ if and only if flatness over $B_{\mathfrak b}$. Under the stalk identifications in step 3, the latter is precisely flatness of $f$ at $z$ by its definition. Thus the chart identifies $E$ with the claimed stalk-flat locus. The only hypotheses used were those in steps 1 and 2; none requires $p$ to be flat.
